quiz_title: AP CS A - Day 10 Exit Quiz: Selection Statements & Scoping
topic: One-Way if Statements, Two-Way if-else Statements, and Block Scoping

questions.question: Consider the following code segment. What is printed as a result of executing this code segment?
questions.explanation: Both if statements are independent. In the first if statement, 15 % 2 == 1 is true and 15 < 20 is true (true && true = true), so "Alpha " is printed. In the second if statement, 15 > 10 is also true, so "Beta" is printed. The total output is "Alpha Beta".

questions.question: Consider the following code segment. What is printed as a result of executing this code segment?
options: A compilation error occurs because of the semicolon after the if condition
questions.explanation: The semicolon immediately following if (val > 15); terminates the if statement with an empty body. The subsequent block { System.out.print("Over limit "); } is treated as an independent block statement that executes unconditionally, followed by printing "Done". Thus, "Over limit Done" is printed.

questions.question: Consider the following code segment. Which of the following best describes what occurs when this code segment is compiled and executed?
options: A compilation error occurs because outcome is not in scope outside the if and else blocks.
A runtime NullPointerException occurs when outcome is evaluated.
questions.explanation: Variables declared inside curly braces { } have local block scope. Both outcome variables exist only within their respective if and else blocks. Attempting to access outcome outside the blocks results in a compilation error because outcome is out of scope.

questions.question: Consider the following code segment with misleading indentation. What is printed as a result of executing this code segment?
questions.explanation: Because curly braces { } are omitted, only the single statement immediately following the if statement (System.out.print("High ");) belongs to the if block. Since count > 10 is false, that statement is skipped. The remaining statements execute sequentially regardless of the if condition, printing "Alert Status".

questions.question: Consider the following code segment. What is printed as a result of executing this code segment?
questions.explanation: In the condition, x / y is 20 / 5 = 4, so 4 == 4 is true. In x % y, 20 % 5 = 0, so 0 == 0 is true. Since true && true evaluates to true, the if branch executes, printing "Divisible ". Because if-else branches are mutually exclusive, the else branch is skipped. Sequential execution then prints "Check completed".
